answer: For a poll on a quill sculpture by the juniper grove, officials randomly draw 100 names from a frozen voter roll. They check submitted photo IDs against the drawn names and count one ballot per match, rejecting mismatches and repeats. Assuming valid IDs, gaining more chances in the draw requires more roll entries, potentially costing recruitment effort. A captured roll can still sway the result, whose ripple may not reflect everyone’s views.
